When you are playing against Stephen Curry, Stephen Curry removes two people from that shell. clips.speaker: Steve Nash
clips.text: Footwork, first and foremost, because it gets you on balance and allows you to get lift. Lift, you got to create force, you got to create power to get the ball up in the air to allow the hand to be soft. Rhythm, that force then creates rhythm. One thing that I think is important is your release point. Some guys have been good at this, I think Jaylen Brown actually sometimes hangs or shoots almost on the way down on his middies. But I think the rule of thumb is you want to shoot as or before you get to the top, because then you're using your legs and you have the same, and it's repeatable.
clips.news_angle: Steve Nash on the importance of footwork for shooting
clips.social_post: Steve Nash explains the importance of footwork and release points, noting that Jaylen Brown sometimes shoots on the way down, but the ideal is to release before the top of the jump.
clips.video_title: LeBron & Steve Nash Reveal the Secrets to Elite Shooting
clips.pull_quote: Footwork, first and foremost, because it gets you on balance and allows you to get lift.

clips.speaker: LeBron James
clips.text: My shooting journey is literally like watching Michael Jordan. But the thing I didn't realize is how balanced Michael Jordan was. I saw a fadeaway. So the flick of the wrist, the head back, I saw a fadeaway. So when I started to see that I had some athletic genes, I maybe picked up some bad habits in my shooting because I can emulate that. So I was shooting fadeaways as like a freshman in high school, and I was making them, but I didn't realize that I was picking up bad habits along that time because I didn't study the fact that, okay, yeah, MJ is doing that, but you're not even seeing how on balance he is.
clips.news_angle: LeBron James on learning to shoot by watching Michael Jordan
clips.social_post: LeBron James admits he picked up bad shooting habits in high school by trying to emulate Michael Jordan fadeaways without understanding the balance behind them.
clips.video_title: LeBron & Steve Nash Reveal the Secrets to Elite Shooting
clips.pull_quote: My shooting journey is literally like watching Michael Jordan.

clips.speaker: LeBron James
clips.text: The detail started, shout out Chris Jent. Elite shooter, played at Ohio State back in the day. He joined Mike Brown when Mike Brown took over in Cleveland early in my years, and I used to watch him shoot in practice. He used to shoot like on the side, or he would be, you know, when the coaches kind of be the scout team sometimes, he would shoot the ball. And even though he's a lefty, it was the same beautiful shot Chris Jent every time, rubbing that, rubbing them ribs, follow through, getting that, getting that arc on it. And I just started to work with him a lot. And it went from during the season to transferring to the off season. So I give a lot of credit to where my shot is today from where it was to Chris Jent.
